title: Talks with US won't happen while interim deal is breached, Iranian minister says
gist: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi says Tehran and Washington are not negotiating and will not while the US breaches the June interim deal, with only intermediary messages passing. An Iran-Oman agreement on the Strait of Hormuz is in its 'final stages' but explicitly will not reopen the waterway: it only pre-defines the shipping lanes to be used once the US meets further conditions.

insights.claim: Iran and the United States are not in negotiations, and Tehran conditions any restart on Washington ceasing its breaches of the interim deal signed in June.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Removes the near-term diplomacy premium from risk pricing: no talks means the Hormuz disruption persists until one side moves first.
insights.quote: Iran and the U.S. are not engaged in talks and Tehran will not start them as long as Washington breaches an interim deal signed in June

insights.claim: Communication between Tehran and Washington continues only as messages passed through intermediaries, not direct contact.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: An intermediary-only channel is slow and deniable — expect headline risk from third-party leaks rather than a clean breakthrough.
insights.quote: adding that messages are being exchanged via intermediaries
insights.locator: adding that messages are being exchanged

insights.claim: Tehran frames the US, not Iran, as the party in violation of the June interim deal, positioning compliance as an American obligation before diplomacy resumes.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: The blame framing signals Iran intends to extract concessions as the price of de-escalation, not to trade reciprocally.
insights.locator: Talks with US won't happen while interim deal is breached

themes.theme: Hormuz deal is not a reopening

insights.claim: The Iran-Oman agreement on the Strait of Hormuz is described as in its 'final stages' yet would not itself reopen the strait to traffic.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Headlines about a near-final Hormuz agreement should not be read as a shipping reopening — the tape can rally on a misread and then reverse.
insights.quote: an agreement on the Strait of Hormuz between Tehran and Muscat was in the "final stages" but would not reopen the strategic waterway

insights.claim: The Iran-Oman agreement's function is to pre-define new shipping lanes that would take effect only after the US fulfils additional Iranian conditions.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Watch for the conditions list, not the lane map: the lanes are pre-agreed plumbing, the conditions are the actual gating item for tanker traffic.
insights.quote: he said the agreement would set out the new shipping lanes to be used once the U.S. fulfils other conditions and the strait is reopened to traffic
insights.locator: In comments reported by Mehr news agency

insights.claim: Oman is Iran's operating counterparty on Hormuz transit arrangements, making Muscat the channel through which any reopening is technically brokered.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Omani statements are the highest-signal leading indicator on Hormuz transit — track Muscat, not Tehran's rhetoric.
insights.locator: an agreement on the Strait of Hormuz between Tehran and Muscat
